text: Automatic Tuning handles sudden, clear-cut regressions on its own. Most regressions aren't that clean — a gradual drift, or one you want to review before anything gets forced. This lesson covers the manual workflow for finding and fixing those.

SSMS's Regressed Queries report, under a database's Query Store folder, ranks queries by declining performance and lets you compare two plan versions side by side, operator by operator — and force the better one directly from that screen.

The same comparison works as scripted T-SQL against Query Store's own catalog views — define a recent window, define a baseline window, and flag queries where recent performance is meaningfully worse. Useful for alerting or automation, not just an interactive report.

The workflow itself is four steps: spot the regression, compare the plans to see if the shape changed or just the stats got worse, decide whether to force a stable better plan or fix the real root cause, then verify the targeted metric actually improved.

This is the measure-identify-change-verify loop from Lesson 1, applied specifically to Query Store data. Next up: running Query Store in production long-term — storage overhead, cleanup policy, and what happens when it fills up.
